⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os validate (command, 83 pages)`
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c88467d4adc417e668474e1b6198a5a7c503ac3f` → `packageMentionDocs`.

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `52b05b8e3211a28c0dc157553d9b8df9c2fe4388`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/lint/src/validate-flow-region-shape.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-flow-region-shape.test.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/flow-region-shape.ts (deleted), packages/cli/src/utils/flow-region-shape.test.ts (deleted), packages/cli/test/authoring-rule-command-parity.test.ts, packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts, packages/cli/test/validate-flow-region-shape.test.ts + packages/spec/src/automation/control-flow.zod.ts (`validateControlFlow`), packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts (`flows: z.array(FlowSchema)`), packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-definitions.ts (`registerFlow`), packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/artifact-packages.ts (`runPerPackageAuthoringRules`, `findingKey`), packages/cli/src/utils/stack-collections.ts (`authoringRuleUnionStack`), packages/lint/src/non-record-object-entry.test.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rule-wiring.test.ts, docs/adr/0031-advanced-flow-node-executors-and-dag.md. Not reviewed: the four `content/docs/**/*.mdx` count bumps and the three `.changeset/*.md` files (read for ②).

### ① Derived judgments

Read on the net diff `origin/main...52b05b8e` and the cited code in the live tree.

- **Accept-set narrowing at `os lint`** — right. A new gating rule `flow-region-shape-invalid` (`tier: 'gating'`, `input: 'parsed'`, `commands: ALL`) runs `FlowSchema.safeParse` then the spec's `validateControlFlow` on every record of `stack.flows`. That is the same two calls `registerFlow` makes (`flow-definitions.ts` lines 213-220: `FlowSchema.parse(converted)`, `detectCycles`, `validateControlFlow(parsed)`); no copy of the region logic exists in the rule. A flow this rule refuses is one the engine refuses to register today, and one `os validate` / `os build` already refused on `main` through the CLI walk. `os lint` goes to the bar the other two commands and the engine already hold; nothing green on `main` under all three commands turns red.
- **Accept set at `os validate` / `os build`** — unchanged, right. The CLI walk (`findFlowRegionRefusals`) walked `packages[]` entries' flows when packages were present, else the stack's own `flows`. The rule reads `stack.flows` only, but the two doors run it over the union stack (`authoringRuleUnionStack` folds `packages[].flows` into an absent top-level `flows`) AND once per package (`runPerPackageAuthoringRules`, where `packageBodyAsStack` puts the package's flows at `flows`), de-duplicated by `findingKey`, which neutralises the top-level index. Coverage is therefore a superset of the walk's: a stack that carries BOTH top-level flows and `packages[]` is now judged on both, where the walk judged only the packages. The case the union fold does not reach (top-level `flows: []` beside packages) is reached by the per-package pass. `os lint` runs the same union + per-package pair (`lint.ts` lines 402, 698, 757), so the assembled-artifact fixture draws one finding at `flows[1]` on all three doors.
- **`--json` row shape for this refusal at `os validate` / `os build`** — changed, right, and unreleased. The old `VALIDATION_ERROR` row with `flow` came from `.changeset/28893-*` and `.changeset/29059-*`, both still pending on `main` (the files exist; a consumed changeset is deleted by Version Packages), so no published consumer reads that shape. The refusal is now an `AuthoringFinding` (`rule`, `where`, `path`, `message`, `hint`) under `errors` (validate) / `issues` (build), the envelope every other gating rule already uses; exit codes and verdicts are unchanged, and the refusal is reported once (the test asserts the count).
- **Public surface of `@objectstack/lint`** — widened, right: `validateFlowRegionShape`, `FLOW_REGION_SHAPE_INVALID`, type `FlowRegionShapeFinding` from the root barrel; `RULE_EXPLANATIONS['flow-region-shape-invalid']` (`covers` 48 chars, no period, three-plus paragraphs: within `rule-explanations.test.ts`' pins). `commands: ALL` satisfies the wiring guard ("every gating rule runs on all three commands"); `surfaces: CLI_ONLY` with a `surfaceReason` over 40 chars satisfies the off-runtime ratchet.
- **Deleted module `packages/cli/src/utils/flow-region-shape.ts`** — right. Internal to `@objectstack/cli` (not a published subpath); no reference to it survives on the branch outside the two pointer comments and the test headers. The `validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` ledger row is removed as that ledger's stale-row check requires; the parity table's `OUTSIDE_THE_TABLE` row moves into `CASES` as its own docblock prescribed, and the empty table goes with it.
- **Fail-closed on a schema-refused flow record** — right, and under `os lint` it is reachable. `lint.ts` hands the `parsed` tier `lowerCallables(authoringRuleUnionStack(normalizeStackInput(config)))`, i.e. the same ADR-0087 D2 conversion layer the other two doors run before their stack parse, so `FlowSchema.safeParse` under lint refuses exactly the flows `stack.zod.ts` (`flows: z.array(FlowSchema)`) would refuse at the `os validate` schema step. A non-record entry (null, string, number, array) is skipped with its index kept, which is what `non-record-object-entry.test.ts` sweeps `stack.flows` with (its junk shapes are null, undefined, string, number, array; `{}` is swept only under `objects`), so the sweep's zero-invented-finding assertion holds for this rule.
- **Rule count 60 to 61 in the four transcripts** — right by construction: exactly one `commands: ALL` entry is added, none scoped.
- **Top-level cycles stay unjudged** — right and declared (rule header, explanation, changeset); `detectCycles` is engine-private and #29051 is open for it.
- **Check-runs on the head: NONE.** `GET commits/52b05b8e/check-runs` returns `total_count: 0`; the five app check-suites (vercel, fly-io, claude, cloudflare, objectstack-fleet) sit `queued` with no conclusion and no GitHub Actions suite is listed (the PR is a draft). So no derived gate family carries a CI verdict on this head yet. The dev's report quotes local readings (lint 7843/7843, cli unit 5263/5263, parity 12/12, spec automation 1745/1745, one ablation that reds the pinned tests and restores clean); those are the dev's claims, consistent with the tree as read, not gate verdicts. The landing conjunct "every check is green" is therefore unmet at the time of this record, independent of its verdict.
- **Dogfood** (owed by the narrowing arm): the dev reports 4 failures (`flow-runas.dogfood.test.ts` x3, `declarative-endpoint-anonymous-guest.dogfood.test.ts` x1) that reproduce identically with lint/cli restored to `origin/main 7b1ae338`; filed as an out-of-scope class-a finding. Not this PR's; read as such.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body and on `.changeset/29049-flow-region-shape-lint-rule.md` (`@objectstack/lint: patch`, `@objectstack/cli: patch`, BREAKING banner, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). Right under ruling A (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, 2026-10-21): the level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` line, and `none` is correct here because no schema, key, default or published symbol of the protocol moves; the spec's own refusal (`validateControlFlow`) is unchanged and merely reaches a third door. A non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner, which this changeset does. The `(narrowing)` arm is declared, as the ADR-0087 gate and the queue guard read it. The ADR-0087 class matches the 28893 changeset's accepted class for the identical change at the other two doors; the body's remedy sentence ("add one node every exit of the region leads to") is the engine's fix for the author's flow, not a consumer code-rewrite prescription.

The two pending changesets `28893-*` and `29059-*` are edited (DELIBERATE CORRECTION class): their sentences about `findFlowRegionRefusals` and a `VALIDATION_ERROR` row would publish false after this PR. The corrected sentences match the tree; restoring them would be wrong. `check-empty-changeset` red on this head is by design and is not a required context; the seat confirms it on the PR.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions 1 — rule id.** Option A, `flow-region-shape-invalid`, is right: subject then verdict, in the registry's existing `-invalid` spelling (`approval-expression-invalid`, `expression-invalid`); B (`-malformed`) says less and C (`-unregisterable`) names the consequence rather than the defect. A name alone is the seat's call; no `needs-user-decision` is owed. The PR body's 维护者速读 line still says the id goes to the maintainer for approval; the dev's deviation names the corrected body r2 for the seat to send. Should-fix on the PR record, not the tree.
- **open_questions 2 — keep fail-closed under `os lint`.** Option A (keep) is right. The engine refuses a flow `FlowSchema` refuses before it ever reaches the region check, so "could not be judged" is a true refusal, not a phantom; `os lint`'s input is the same normalized stack the other doors parse, so the finding fires on exactly the flows `os validate` refuses at its schema step (no false refusal of a flow the engine registers); and option B would reopen the silent-pass branch #29059 closed at validate/build, since the rule cannot tell which command runs it. The finding names the cause ("the flow schema refused it", with the schema's issues) and the hint points at `os validate`, so the rule id's `region shape` wording does not mislead. No change.
- **Deviation: runtime publish surface left `CLI_ONLY`.** In contract: `surfaceReason` names #29233 (open, p2, `domain:server`, dispatched), which will put `validateControlFlow` into `runtime-authoring-gate.ts` at the publish door. Should-fix carried to #29233, not here: when that lands, this entry's reason goes stale, and the cheaper shape is to wire THIS rule (`surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `runtimeTypes: ['flow']`, as `lintFlowPatterns` and `validateFlowTriggerReadiness` are) rather than a second call at the gate, so one registry row answers both doors.
- **Deviation: MCP assignee/reviewer skipped** — right; the standard order forbids it.
- **Deviation: `--json` row shape** — judged in ①: unreleased shape, no consumer.
- **Out-of-scope findings**: dogfood 4 red on `main` (class a, main-red candidate, not bisected) and the top-level cycle (#29051) — both correctly left to their carriers; the first needs a card if none exists.
- Nothing escalates to the maintainer from this record.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing read against the published spec on `main`: `packages/spec/src/automation/control-flow.zod.ts` `validateControlFlow` throws on a region that is not single-entry/single-exit, on a cyclic region body, and on a `parallel` with fewer than two branches, and `parseFlowNodeRegions` deliberately leaves a malformed region raw "for `validateControlFlow` to name" — the spec's own stated refusal, which ADR-0031 declares (lines 75, 122, 174). `registerFlow` runs it on every flow. So the capability the author holds under the spec is "a flow whose regions are single-entry/single-exit, acyclic, with two-plus parallel branches"; a flow outside that was never registered and never ran. This PR takes no declared capability away at the consumer: it makes the spec's own refusal real at the one authoring door that was still blind to it, with the spec's own function and sentence. That is the #4409 contract (three commands, one verdict) applied to a rule that #28893 had wired to two.

Attempts to break it, each read in the tree:

- *Does the rule refuse under `os lint` what the engine registers?* No: `registerFlow` applies conversions with `includeRetired: true` only for the stored-row rehydration seam; an AUTHORED stack reaches `FlowSchema` through `normalizeStackInput` on every door, and the rule reads that same normalized body under lint. The retired-alias case is refused by the schema on every door alike.
- *Does moving from the walk to the rule table lose a flow?* No: union fold plus per-package pass is a superset of the walk's subject set (①), and the de-dup key collapses the echo so the assembled case draws one row, as the test pins on all three doors.
- *Does the rule throw on junk?* No: `isRec` skips non-records and `FlowSchema.safeParse` never throws; the family sweep's shapes for `flows` are all non-records.
- *Does the schema-refused branch invent a finding?* Only for a record `FlowSchema` refuses, which `os validate` refuses at its schema step and the engine refuses at registration; both directions hold.
- *Does the `input: 'parsed'` tier starve the rule under lint?* No: `runAuthoringRules` hands `run.parsed ?? run.normalized`, and `lint.ts` passes `parsed: lowered`.
- *Is the deleted walk cited anywhere that now dangles?* No: no `flow-region-shape.ts` / `findFlowRegionRefusals` reference survives in `content/`, `skills/`, `docs/`, `.claude/` or `packages/` outside the two pointer comments and the test headers that record the move.

Must-fix: none.

Should-fix (none blocks):
1. PR body 维护者速读 still routes the rule id to the maintainer as `needs-user-decision`; send the r2 body (seat; not the tree).
2. Carried to #29233: wire the publish door through this registry row (`CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `runtimeTypes: ['flow']`) rather than a parallel `validateControlFlow` call at the gate, and retire this entry's `surfaceReason` in the same stroke.

Nothing in the tree is judged on the PR body's account of it; the readings above are from the diff and the cited code. The head carries no check-run yet (①): this PASS is a verdict on the contract and the design, and the queue's own "every check green" conjunct still has to be met on `52b05b8e` before the seat lands it.
